CROW CULTURE
Crow Religion
Crow legend ascribes the creation of the world to a culture hero/trickster called Old Man Coyote. The first medicine or power Old Man Coyote gave to the Crows was the sweat bath, which is a small domed lodge constructed with willows and covered with hides. Hot stones are placed in a pit inside the lodge and water is poured over them, creating a very hot steam to cleanse the bathers. The sweat bath was used only for religious purposes and came before all important ceremonials and undertakings. The lodge represents the first Maker's body. In addition to the sweat bath, servants or helpers of Old Man Coyote taught the Sun Dance, Tobacco Ceremony and the Rock Medicines. Thus the number four has been considered sacred. Four poles are used as a base for erecting the sweat lodge and tepees and the number appears in most traditional ceremonial events. The sweat hut today is being used mainly as a religious event, as well as being used for treating ailments.
Crows were taught how to make and use medicine bundles; the importance of all animals, objects of nature and how to obtain good things in life from within nature's powers. Of all possessions the medicine bundle was the most important and valuable for contained within each bundle were objects given to the individual by certain persons from another
